title: My Program to go BERSERKER MODE (BODYBUILDING GOAL PHYSIQUE)
summary: NH walks through his personal 8-day gentleman's split for a 'berserker' physique (big limbs and core, minimal shoulders and chest), built around nucleus overload for forearms, calves, triceps and lats, nonstop giant sets and rotating interchangeable lines. He warns it is too specialized for others and uses it to teach flexible programming, mirror days and goal-physique-driven design.
claims: His personal program is not for others: it is too specialized, will overwork the average lifter and create imbalances they do not have
The berserker physique emphasizes limbs and core and de-emphasizes shoulders and chest; his shoulders are smaller than a year ago on purpose
His goal physique mixes Zodd and Guts from Berserk, Uvogin from Hunter x Hunter and Toguro; Guts has too much shoulder development for his taste
The program is an 8-day gentleman's (body-part) split trained 6 days a week
Nucleus overload is applied to his priority muscles: forearms, calves, triceps and lats, via pullovers, finger curls, towel curls, calf and triceps work, plus dumbbells for the upper back
Neck, abs and traps get no nucleus overload but are trained to failure at high frequency: neck every 2 days, abs daily, traps every 3-4 days

claims.frequency: neck every 2 days, abs daily, traps every 3-4 days

claims: He has very short clavicles so his traps pop easily; he avoids blowing them up so they do not look ridiculous
He builds programs starting from muscles, calling himself a muscle split junkie
Days are Upper 1/2 (press focus), Squat 1/2 (knee flexion), Arms 1/2 and Deadlift 1/2 (hip hinge); arm days are 25% of the program
Rigid splits are mostly idiotic; he puts calf work on upper days and grip work on squat days because there is room
He sees a program as a rotating pyramid: strong base and walls, but each piece can be swapped while it stays a pyramid
He never does every line of a day, only 2-4 lines, selected by what needs work; doing it all would be junk volume
Everything is done as nonstop giant sets with no rest between exercises, for time efficiency, after building the conditioning for it
Alternating upper and lower means leg day every 48 hours, and calves have a slot on every day of the 8
His biggest calf mistake was waiting for the perfect moment to train them; the right moment is now
Calves get light nucleus overload on upper days and heavy Toshiki raises on lower days
If his lower back is tired after SSB box squats he swaps good mornings for hip thrusts to train the posterior chain without spinal loading
He never deloads because rotating muscles and lifts manages recovery
Adopting someone else's self-made program usually yields no gains; that is why many respected youtubers refuse to share theirs
His previous program stagnated for two years; instead of blaming genetics he blamed its lack of flexibility
Novices need rigid structure, but intermediates must embrace freedom; the more advanced, the stranger and more day-to-day flexible the program should be
Shoulder work is minimal and chest is mostly on the two upper days; the tonnage saved goes into arms, especially forearms
His triceps long head has caught up with his biceps, so he is now recreating the imbalance by focusing on biceps
He does two ring days per 8-day cycle; rings are a good supplement but doing only rings for arms would be foolish
Pullovers developed his lats a lot, so he is slowing down on them
Exercises within a day are optional; he skips ones he does not want, since he is the master of his program, like a bamboo bending rather than an oak breaking
Nucleus overload rarely takes away from recovery and even helps; even a minimal amount is worth doing
Mirror days repeat a day's muscle emphasis with different lifts for rotation and fewer overuse injuries; build the second from the first, and novices do not need them
He partly needs many mirror-day exercises simply to avoid boredom with lifts that work for him
Followers of his programs can cut exercises or volume freely; you are the captain of your own ship
The best program is one you made yourself, aligned with a goal physique, often drawn from fictional characters
exercises: superset with pseudo-dragonflies and nucleus overload
heavy calf raise on lower days
replace good mornings when lower back is tired
